Disease Outbreak Impacts Medical Equipment & Devices Industry Workforce in Madagascar

Antananarivo – A respiratory illness outbreak has struck multiple facilities belonging to the Medical Equipment & Devices industry in Madagascar, causing significant disruption to production and staffing. The outbreak, first identified last week at a syringe assembly plant operated by MadaMed Solutions in Toamasina, has now affected staff at three additional sites in Antananarivo and Mahajanga.

Industry sources report more than 120 confirmed cases of the illness among workers so far, with symptoms including fever, cough, and shortness of breath. Many affected staff are currently under medical observation or required to isolate at home, resulting in a sharp reduction in available personnel across manufacturing, quality control, and maintenance teams.

“We are doing everything possible to ensure the safety of our employees,” said Jean Rakotoarisoa, spokesperson for the Madagascar Medical Devices Manufacturers Association. “Production has slowed as we deep-clean sites and implement new health protocols. However, worker health remains our top priority.”

Several companies have temporarily suspended operations on certain assembly lines, while others have staggered shifts to reduce contact among workers. According to a union representative, “Employees are worried, but management has been transparent about the situation and is providing regular updates.”

The full impact on industry output remains unclear, but analysts say that with the outbreak ongoing, firms are likely to face continued challenges in meeting targets. “The current situation is unprecedented for Madagascar’s medical devices sector,” noted analyst Haja Raveloson. “Recovery will depend on how quickly the outbreak is contained and normal staffing levels can be restored.”

Health authorities are working closely with affected companies to monitor the situation.
